questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to France but not Paris and then Toulouse was a possibility, that seemed nice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved the city and the people i meet, but the university is not good. The university is really demanding, some days the classes ended at 20.00.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult a lot of the information is in french. But the international office at the university were good at answering mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance when I arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were one introduction day and then you were supposed to figure out the rest by yourself. Luckily there were a lot of other exchange students so we figured it out together.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: When you apply you just mark that you want student housing and then you are secured a place. It is not possible to apply for a specific campus when you apply. So I didn't live on the campus for my university but on a campus for another university 30 min away from my university.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a small kitchen in my room. There were also cafeterias and canteens on the campus where you could eat.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very small rooms and you do not know were in the city you will get a room. Student housing in Toulouse is very cheap around 250 euro per month in 2024.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a little confusing and some of the classes that I had planned on taking overlapped so I had to take some other classes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The classes start and the you have around 2 weeks to try different classes and figure out which you want to take. There is no introduction days or something you have to follow the classes and then at the same time try to figure out which classes you are taking.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a student counsellor that you could email or plan a meeting with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is going to be some changes in the learning agreement, so be prepared to make changes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very demanding and the classes were some days ending at 20.00. The ECTS point didn't correspond to how much were expected from the students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of some of the MA courses was too difficult for BA students. Some of the courses were very specific extensions on courses the locals had had the semester before.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The way they study in France is a lot different from how we study in Denmark. For the written exams it is expected that you remember everything by heart. Most of the courses is only lectures. In some courses there are presentations that count for the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Development economics, Economie du climat, Environmental and ressource economics, Industruial organisation, Market finance and Topics in food economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Environmental and resource economics and topics in food economics because there were a good mix of both lectures and group work. Development economics was also interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was not unexpected but it is a good idea to count travelling to other cities in the budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grosery shopping was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to do sports for free through the university and Crous. The university also has drawing, acting and other cultural events however it is mostly in French.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did some sports at the university which was nice and also an opportunity to talk to the locals. Otherwise, I would recommend to follow ESN Toulouse on Instagram and join the Erasmus groups on WhatsApp to see what is happening.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend to go around in the south of France. In paticular, I would recommend to go to spend some days in Marseille and also in Bordeaux. There are a lot of nice small cities around Toulouse. If you want to go to the sea Montpeiller, Sete and Collioure are nice cities. I also went to Barcelona which is around 6 hours away in bus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy I didn't really think about it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As mentioned before it is a good idea to join a sport or something. But in general, it is difficult to become friends with the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything particularly challenging. I could imagine that the language could be challenging because a lot only speak Frenc. But I speak a little French and it went fine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Many different things

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It is confusing in the beginning with course selection
2. They demand a lot in all of the courses
3. They are still using paper and pen

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun. But also take studying seriously.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing people I have met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period all exams are in 2 weeks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
